description: §48.2 — a `fn`/`function` declaration with an `=` EXPRESSION body (`fn pick(k) -> bool = match k {…}`) is NOT a sanctioned scrml shape and SHALL fire E-FN-EQUALS-BODY at parse. The grammar admits exactly one body form: a `{ … }` block (`fn-body ::= '{' fn-statement* '}'`). Sibling of the `=>`-arrow reject (E-FN-ARROW-BODY, §48.2.1). Regression guard: pre-fix the `-> T = <expr>` return-type consumer swallowed `bool = match k` and the match's `{` was misread as the body brace, so the match arms parsed as loose statements — arm TEST literals emitted as bare `1;`, arm RESULTS dropped, the fn returning `undefined` with ZERO diagnostics (HIGH silent-wrong-output); the `= if` variant instead reached E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC.
rationale: §48.2: `fn-body ::= '{' fn-statement* '}'` — the block body is the only sanctioned body form. A one-expression function is written `fn f(args) { return <expr> }`, or `fn f(args) { <expr> }` (a block body implicitly returns its tail expression). The `= <expr>` form is unsanctioned and is rejected at parse with E-FN-EQUALS-BODY, which steers to the block form and cross-references the `=>`-arrow sibling E-FN-ARROW-BODY.
